findings.summary: The mobile layout renders a 1,024 px desktop canvas inside a 360 px viewport.
findings.evidence: The mobile layout primitive reports scrollWidth 1024, visualViewportWidth 360, and 664 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot shows clipped navigation and content.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace fixed desktop widths with intrinsic/fluid layout and verify every template at narrow widths without horizontal overflow.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow, zoom policy, and target sizing fail accessibility expectations.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails meta-viewport and target-size; layout evidence shows 664 px overflow at 360 px.
findings.suggestedFix: Permit user scaling, reflow at 320 CSS px, and enlarge/space controls to accessible target sizes.

findings.summary: Important controls and text do not survive enhanced-contrast needs.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports contrast ratios as low as 1.75:1 on the age-verification banner and 3.29:1 on view counts; the high-contrast capture does not introduce a stronger theme.
findings.suggestedFix: Use contrast-safe tokens and forced-colors/prefers-contrast overrides for text and controls.

findings.summary: A full-screen consent overlay obscures every audited content route on first load.
findings.evidence: Homepage, categories, search, video, and signup captures all show the same 780×493 fixed consent layer covering the primary content before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-obscuring consent surface where legally possible; persist the decision promptly and preserve equivalent Accept/Reject actions.

findings.summary: The consent modal lacks dialog semantics.
findings.evidence: The overlay probe found the visible fixed consent surface with no role or aria-modal; the page has zero dialog and popover elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog> or role=dialog/aria-modal, an accessible name, focus trapping, Escape handling, and focus restoration.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch sizing are unreliable.
findings.evidence: The probe counted 52 controls smaller than 24 px and found many focused controls with outline-style none/0 px; Lighthouse also fails target-size.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide visible :focus-visible rings and at least 44×44 CSS-pixel touch targets or sufficient spacing.

findings.summary: Mobile loading misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured FCP 3.5 s and LCP 3.8 s; the trace measured LCP 2.26 s in a separate run, showing the mobile result is the risk condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, reduce render-blocking CSS, and defer non-critical scripts.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and dependency chains delay first content.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,210 ms savings from render-blocking requests; HAR confirms three VeryHigh parser-inserted stylesheets and 151 requests.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, defer non-critical styles, preserve async/defer on scripts, and tighten cache lifetimes.

findings.summary: Interactive controls and signup fields lack robust accessible names and labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse finds two unnamed buttons and label/content-name mismatches; the email signup state exposes email/password inputs with zero associated labels.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every control a programmatic name matching visible text and associate persistent labels with signup fields.

findings.summary: Multiple text surfaces fail WCAG contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identifies age-banner text at 1.75:1 and 2.15:1 and metadata at 3.29:1 against dark surfaces.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background token pairs to meet WCAG AA in every theme and state.

findings.summary: Focus visibility and list structure are not consistently accessible.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found key controls with no outline/box-shadow and Lighthouse reports malformed list content plus an accessibility-tree failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore semantic list structure, establish landmarks/headings, and add a clear focus-visible treatment with logical order.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP transport protections are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS/HSTS are present, but CSP is only frame-ancestors; four of five cookies lack Secure and several use SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a restrictive CSP, mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, and use the strictest viable SameSite/HttpOnly settings.

findings.summary: The initial load has a broad third-party footprint before consent.
findings.evidence: HAR records 117 third-party requests and 1.65 MB transferred from third-party origins; tracker evidence finds 12 third-party origins, including ad and Google account endpoints.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential third parties until consent/interaction, minimise identifiers, and batch/defer analytics and recommendations.

findings.summary: Defensive response policies are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers lack X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy; CSP contains only frame-ancestors and Permissions-Policy allows only client hints rather than constraining sensitive features.
findings.suggestedFix: Add nosniff, a strict referrer policy, capability-limiting Permissions-Policy, and a full CSP with script/style/connect directives.

findings.summary: Email signup fields do not expose robust validation semantics.
findings.evidence: After selecting email signup, email/password fields have no labels, required=false, and no aria-invalid state; error timing and announcement affordances are absent from the initial form state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use required constraints, persistent labels, :user-invalid after interaction, and an announced error summary.

findings.summary: Signup obstructs autofill for email.
findings.evidence: Both email inputs report autocomplete="off" while the password correctly uses new-password.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="email" and keep new-password; use stable names and labels so password managers can assist.

findings.summary: Third-party code dominates the page budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 117/151 requests and 1.65/1.78 MB transferred; static CDN JavaScript alone includes a 400 KB entry bundle.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party budget, lazy-load partner widgets, and remove providers that do not justify their byte/privacy cost.

findings.summary: The site does not follow the system color-scheme preference.
findings.evidence: Light and dark emulation screenshots are visually equivalent and the platform probe reports computed colorScheme “normal”.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, eight animations remain running with 2000 ms durations.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a reduced-motion media query that removes non-essential transitions and looping/preview motion.

findings.summary: Promotional chrome competes heavily with primary content.
findings.evidence: Desktop captures stack two navigation rows, age verification, a seasonal promotion, side navigation, partner promotions, and consent over the content grid.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate promotions and defer secondary partner modules so the content/task occupies most of the first viewport.

findings.summary: Reusable cards and navigation do not adapt at component level.
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe found no @container rules, while the 360 px capture keeps desktop sidebar/card geometry and clips the result grid.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable regions and size-aware @container rules for cards, filters, and navigation.

findings.summary: The entry page ships avoidable CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 56 KiB unused CSS and 26 KiB unused JavaScript; HAR records 66 scripts and 1.02 MB script transfer.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split by template, remove dead CSS, and load third-party/account modules only on demand.

findings.summary: Narrow-screen clipping and low-contrast metadata harm legibility.
findings.evidence: At 360 px, the desktop canvas clips headings, navigation, and card text; Lighthouse reports 12 px view metadata at 3.29:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow text to reflow, remove fixed-width clipping, and use readable size/line-height/contrast tokens.

findings.summary: Most images lack intrinsic dimensions and several are oversized.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports 29/36 images without width/height and 13 oversized images, although the document has a valid doctype and UTF-8 charset.
findings.suggestedFix: Set width/height or aspect-ratio and deliver the responsive candidate closest to rendered size.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and platform hygiene warnings remain.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three deprecation warnings and a best-practices score of 0.81.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API usage and address DevTools/Lighthouse inspector warnings before they become compatibility failures.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are incomplete across a large multilingual catalog.
findings.evidence: Canonical URLs and robots.txt are present, but /sitemap.xml returns 404 and no hreflang links were found on English or German templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish sitemap indexes and reciprocal hreflang links aligned with canonical URLs and robots policy.

findings.summary: Video entities lack structured VideoObject data.
findings.evidence: The representative video has Open Graph/Twitter metadata but zero JSON-LD blocks, so crawlers must infer video properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org VideoObject JSON-LD matching the visible title, thumbnail, duration, upload date, and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Runtime overlays and fixed layout do not remain robust at narrow sizes.
findings.evidence: The visible consent layer is a custom fixed 780×493 element without dialog semantics, while the 360 px page retains 1,024 px layout width.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic top-layer UI and intrinsic sizing so overlays, menus, and state remain usable at every viewport edge.

findings.summary: Image delivery wastes bytes on oversized and legacy candidates.
findings.evidence: The image audit reports 13 oversized images, 15 legacy-format images, 29 missing dimensions, and 8 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve right-sized AVIF/WebP through srcset/sizes, reserve dimensions, and lazy-load below-fold media.

findings.summary: The homepage performs disproportionate background/network work before interaction.
findings.evidence: The initial load makes 151 requests, runs 66 scripts, and transfers 1.78 MB before the user chooses consent or starts media.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer recommendation, account, ad, and preview modules until visible or requested and deprioritise background fetches.

findings.summary: Repeated feed traversal retains measurable heap growth.
findings.evidence: After 10 bottom/top traversals, heap grows from 710,431 to 734,398 nodes and 37.62 MB to 39.20 MB (+1.58 MB); separate fresh-page captures make this medium-confidence rather than proof of a leak.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the repeated feed interaction in one long-lived session, release offscreen preview/card state, and verify growth plateaus.

findings.summary: The landing page has a large initial object/DOM footprint.
findings.evidence: The baseline heap contains 710,431 nodes, 3.34 million edges, 95,643 closures, and 37.62 MB self size before media playback.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial card/module population, virtualise long lists, and delay non-visible component construction.

findings.summary: Repeated scrolling leaves substantial native and closure growth that needs leak investigation.
findings.evidence: The post snapshot has +9,274 native nodes and +4,003 closures; no Detached* constructor appears in the compact top list, so the signal is accumulation risk rather than a confirmed detached-DOM leak.
findings.suggestedFix: Instrument listeners/observers and preview timers during repeated traversal, dispose them on card teardown, and confirm closure/native counts plateau.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not use authored View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The platform supports document.startViewTransition, but the CSS/DOM probe found no view-transition rules across the entry surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route and major state changes with same- or cross-document View Transitions and a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: The long listing has static chrome without scroll-state feedback.
findings.evidence: The homepage is 4,486 px tall, while the platform probe found no scroll-timeline or container-query support and the mobile capture retains desktop-style fixed chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state/container queries or a lightweight progress/compact-header treatment to preserve orientation.

findings.summary: Menus and overlays rely on physical positioning rather than anchor-aware placement.
findings.evidence: Rendered CSS inspection found physical left/right positioning throughout and no anchor-positioning declarations; overlays are custom fixed elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Use CSS anchor positioning with position-try fallbacks for menus and contextual overlays.
